solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dog daughter found in Dorset town

indicators.note: something found in a place sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Poole is a coastal town in Dorset, a county in southern England
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A dog's daughter, or a girl's dog, turns up in a seaside town in Dorset.
explanation.walkthrough: D goes inside POOLE to give POODLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A poodle is a breed of dog with a curly coat.

clue.text: One criminal originally arrested by European constabulary

indicators.note: someone arrested is held by another, so these pieces are held inside the outer word

parts.note: a Pole is a person from Poland
the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: originally points to the start of the word, so only its opening letter is used

parts.note: first letter of criminal

explanation.surface: A lone offender is caught by a European police force.
explanation.walkthrough: I and C go inside POLE to give POLICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A constabulary is a police force, so the two words name the same body of officers.

clue.text: Living in car, go all over the place

indicators.note: things all over the place are scattered in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone living out of their car, driving aimlessly around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic describes matter that is or was alive, a sense synonymous with living.

clue.text: Many nicked, almost all turning up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the letters are read from bottom to top
almost all of a word means it loses its final letter

parts.note: nicked is British slang for stolen, so stole

explanation.surface: Lots of stolen goods, nearly all of it, reappear.
explanation.walkthrough: STOLE drops its last letter to STOL, which then reads upwards. To nick is everyday British slang for to steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lots, as in 'lots of people', is a plural quantity word meaning a large number, like many.

clue.text: Wife has rings: that was careless!

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for wife
hoops are rings

explanation.surface: A wife drops her rings and admits her clumsiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoops is the exclamation people make after a careless slip or small accident.

clue.text: Restrain worker on strike

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
to cuff is to strike with the open hand
joins the two pieces, the second following the first

explanation.surface: Hold back an employee who is out on strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' suggests industrial action, but here it is a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: To handcuff someone is to restrain them by locking their wrists together.

clue.text: Old giant, Greek character

parts.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
mega means huge

explanation.surface: An ancient giant from Greek mythology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' hints at a mythological figure; it is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, and letters are characters.

clue.text: Pip kidnapping Queen, get angry

indicators.note: a kidnapper holds a captive, so one word is held within the other

parts.note: a pip is a fruit seed
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword queen

explanation.surface: Pip, perhaps the Dickens hero, abducts the Queen and loses his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: Pip suggests the boy hero of Dickens's Great Expectations, but here it is the seed of a fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To see red is an idiom for becoming suddenly furious.

clue.text: Smoker's accessory easier to carry?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a device for igniting cigarettes

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark makes it look like one thought about a handy pocket gadget, but there are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the noun for a flame-making gadget and the comparative adjective of light, meaning less heavy.

clue.text: Fresh procedure for clone

indicators.note: fresh means new or remade, so the letters are formed into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A new laboratory method for cloning an organism.
explanation.definitionFit: To clone something is to make an exact copy of it, which is to reproduce it.

clue.text: Relative in Greece I need to return

indicators.note: returning goes back the way it came, so the letters are read right to left
in says the letters sit inside the following words

parts.note: letters spanning the end of Greece, the I and the start of need

explanation.surface: A relative living in Greece whom I need to bring home.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a family member, the daughter of a sibling.

clue.text: Bit of money delivered, by the sound of it?

indicators.note: this tells us the answer is what we hear when the clue word is spoken

parts.note: delivered means sent

explanation.surface: A coin has been delivered, or so it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: A cent is a small coin, one hundredth of a dollar or euro.

clue.text: Herb keeps step in modern times

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold onto it, so one word holds the other inside

parts.note: sage is a herb
a pace is a step

explanation.surface: A herb that keeps pace with the times.
explanation.walkthrough: The enumeration (5,3) splits the result into two words once the herb holds the step.
explanation.definitionFit: The space age is the present era of spaceflight, a term for the modern period.

clue.text: Items are designed in Abu Dhabi etc

indicators.note: something designed is planned and constructed, so the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Goods designed in the Gulf states.
explanation.definitionFit: Abu Dhabi is one of the seven emirates of the UAE; 'etc' makes the definition plural, so it names those states.

clue.text: Oh please, get down from there!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an exclamation of disbelief
second meaning, taken literally: a command to climb off something

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a single exasperated order to a child climbing furniture; the phrase is both a scoff at nonsense and a literal instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is said to someone talking rubbish, much like 'oh please', and literally tells someone to descend.

clue.text: Spear I'd thrown in river

indicators.note: something thrown in lands inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: the Trent is a major river in the English Midlands
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man confesses to hurling a spear into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown' looks like the spear's action, perhaps an anagram signal, but with 'in' it puts one piece inside the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A trident is a three-pronged spear, like Neptune's.

clue.text: Set of thirteen cards passed around

indicators.note: around suggests moving about and changing position, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A hand of cards is dealt round the table.
explanation.definitionFit: Spades is one of the four suits in a standard pack, each suit having thirteen cards.

clue.text: Accommodation found in chalet, so hard up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top
found in says the letters are inside the following words

parts.note: letters spanning the end of chalet, so, and the start of hard

explanation.surface: A ski chalet where the money is tight.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostel is cheap lodging, a kind of accommodation for travellers.

clue.text: Sulk about crew backing blackout

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: to pout is to sulk

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so this word is read right to left

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sulking because the crew supports a news blackout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blackout' suggests censorship but here means loss of electricity, and 'backing' means going backwards, not support.
explanation.definitionFit: A blackout is a failure of the electricity supply, which is a power cut.

clue.text: Bet it's time to wear coat for winter

indicators.note: to here means going into, so one piece is put inside the other
a coat is the outside layer, so only the outermost letters of the word are kept

parts.note: the outside letters of wear
an age is a period of time
surface padding that sets the wintry scene and adds no letters

explanation.surface: Betting that cold weather means it is time to put a coat on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coat' reads as clothing, but it asks for the outer layer of wear, which wraps around the time word.
explanation.definitionFit: A wager is a bet, a stake placed on an outcome.

clue.text: Initially coming in, also out — "hi" or 'bye"!

indicators.note: initially points to the start of each following word, so only opening letters are used

parts.note: first letters of coming, in, also and out

explanation.surface: Greeting people as they come and go.
explanation.definitionFit: Ciao is an informal Italian word used both as hello and as goodbye.

clue.text: Cheese, if the worst, gorgonzola last of all

indicators.note: last of all asks for the final letter of every word in the run

parts.note: last letters of if, the, worst and gorgonzola

explanation.surface: Choosing a cheese: if the worst comes to it, gorgonzola is the last resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Gorgonzola invites the solver to think of the answer as that cheese, but it only supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is a white Greek cheese made from sheep's or goat's milk.

clue.text: Finger, for example, like it

parts.note: to dig something is slang for liking it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Pointing a finger and approving: like it.
explanation.definitionFit: A digit is a finger or toe; a finger is one example of it.

clue.text: Mountain most steep, though not the first

indicators.note: not the first says the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: severest means harshest, here steepest

explanation.surface: A mountain that is the steepest climb, yet not the highest ranked.
explanation.definitionFit: Everest, in the Himalayas, is the world's highest mountain.

clue.text: Place importance on anxiety

explanation.surface: Someone who makes too much of their worries.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to emphasise, and the noun means worry or tension.

clue.text: Alter reforms attached to Conservative business association

indicators.note: to reform something is to reshape it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A Conservative government changes the rules for a business group.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartel is a group of firms that agree to fix prices or output, a kind of trade association.
